batch_metadata.description: Additional verse dramas in the tradition of the Ivory Renaissance. These works explore noble downfall, territorial disputes, and archival betrayals.

books.title: The Fall of Duchess Mammontine
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: A duchess loses her ancestral library to fire after refusing to share its contents with rival houses. The play examines the tension between preservation and hoarding.
books.notes: Tuskfall's only completed tragedy. She died during the plague of 1658.

books.title: The Exile of Baron Probost
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Baron Probost is banished for falsifying records in the Archive. His attempts to prove his innocence only deepen suspicion of his motives.
books.notes: Greyprob based the plot on a real scandal from 1639.

books.title: Lorde Trumpington's Debt
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: A lord mortgages his family's archive to finance a war. When the debt comes due, he must choose between honor and the preservation of ancestral records.
books.notes: Performed during the height of the Border Wars. Controversial for its critique of military spending.

books.title: The Silence of Lady Dermaine
books.author: R. Trumpelder
books.summary: Lady Dermaine witnesses a murder in the Archive but takes a vow of silence to protect her family. The play explores the weight of unspoken knowledge.
books.notes: Trumpelder's darkest work. Rarely performed due to its bleak ending.

books.title: The Betrayal of Count Stompwell
books.author: J. Stompberton
books.summary: A count discovers his most trusted advisor has been selling archive secrets to enemy houses. The betrayal forces him to question all his alliances.
books.notes: Stompberton studied under J. Temberton. The influence is evident in the sparse dialogue.

books.title: Duchess Ivoreth's Inheritance
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: A duchess inherits a library filled with forbidden texts. She must decide whether to preserve or destroy knowledge deemed dangerous by the Crown.
books.notes: Greyhorn's late-career work. The themes of censorship reflect her own struggles with authorities.

books.title: The Ruin of Viscount Trunsworth
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Viscount Trunsworth bankrupts his estate to acquire a legendary manuscript. When the manuscript proves to be a forgery, his house falls into disgrace.
books.notes: Tuskfall's final work before her death. Unfinished in places.

books.title: The Disgrace of Baron Trunkard
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: A baron is accused of destroying records that implicate his family in past crimes. His defense rests on proving the records never existed.
books.notes: One of Wryte's banned works. Not published openly until 1710.

books.title: Lorde Trunmere's Oath
books.author: R. Trumpelder
books.summary: A lord swears to recover stolen family records. His quest becomes an obsession that destroys his relationships and ultimately his sanity.
books.notes: Features an extended mad scene considered one of the finest in Renaissance drama.

books.title: The Ashes of Countess Greyvane
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Countess Greyvane burns her own archive to prevent it from falling into enemy hands during a siege. The play questions whether destruction can be an act of preservation.
books.notes: Written during the Border Wars. Reflects the anxiety of the era.

books.title: The Weeping of Duke Pachara
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: A duke mourns the loss of his family's oral traditions after the last elder dies without passing them on. The play explores memory as a fragile, mortal thing.
books.notes: Greyprob's most personal work. His own family lost many oral histories during the plague.

books.title: Regent Ivornne's Trial
books.author: J. Stompberton
books.summary: A regent is put on trial for allowing restricted texts to be read by commoners. The trial becomes a debate about who has the right to knowledge.
books.notes: Banned in several provinces for its populist sympathies.

books.title: The Doom of Lady Elaphoria
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Elaphoria refuses to marry to save her family's archive. Her defiance leads to her house's dissolution and the scattering of its records.
books.notes: Wryte's most explicitly feminist work. Caused significant scandal.

books.title: The Unmaking of Baron Pachmont
books.author: R. Trumpelder
books.summary: A baron's identity is erased when all records of his lineage are destroyed in a fire. The play explores whether one can exist without documented history.
books.notes: Trumpelder's most philosophical tragedy. Influenced later existential works.

books.title: Count Tuskmont's Last Stand
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Count Tuskmont defends his archive against raiders. The siege becomes a meditation on the value of preservation versus survival.
books.notes: Greyhorn's penultimate work. The battle scenes are remarkably vivid.

books.title: The Pride of Lorde Mammorek
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Lorde Mammorek refuses to admit errors in his family's genealogical records. His stubbornness leads rival houses to question the legitimacy of his entire lineage.
books.notes: Temberton's examination of pride and record-keeping. The verse is unusually compressed.

books.title: Duchess Trunkmore's Confession
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: A duchess reveals that half the documents in her family archive are fabrications created by her grandfather. The confession threatens to destabilize the entire nobility.
books.notes: Considered Tuskfall's masterpiece. The confession scene is twenty pages of unbroken verse.

books.title: The Madness of Baron Greytrunk
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Baron Greytrunk becomes obsessed with finding a single missing page from an ancient census. His search consumes his fortune and alienates his family.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's darkest work. The baron's deterioration mirrors that of King Elephas III.

books.title: Lady Probshire's Gambit
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Probshire wages a legal war over archive rights after her husband's death. Her campaign reveals that women's contributions to record-keeping are systematically erased.
books.notes: Wryte's most political tragedy. Inspired reforms to inheritance law in three provinces.

books.title: The Census of Count Ivordale
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Count Ivordale conducts a secret census of his lands, only to discover that his own scribes have been falsifying population records for decades.
books.notes: Based on the infamous Census Scandal of 1652. Greyprob interviewed surviving participants.

books.title: Viscount Tuskwell's Heir
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: A viscount discovers his adopted heir has been stealing and selling family documents. The betrayal forces him to choose between love and duty.
books.notes: Greyhorn's most tender tragedy. The final confrontation is heartbreaking in its restraint.

books.title: The Forgeries of Duchess Mammoline
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Duchess Mammoline commissions forged land deeds to reclaim ancestral territory. Her scheme unravels when the forger demands payment in forbidden manuscripts.
books.notes: Temberton's most complex plot. Features three distinct forgeries, each exposed differently.

books.title: Lorde Pachoral's Dilemma
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: A lord must choose between executing a scribe who revealed state secrets and protecting the principle of archival transparency.
books.notes: The ethical debate forms the center of the play. No clear answer is offered.

books.title: The Silence of Baron Trumwood
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Baron Trumwood knows which rival house burned the Royal Archive but refuses to name them. His silence is both loyalty and cowardice.
books.notes: Mammorthorn explores the consequences of protected knowledge. The baron never speaks after the second scene.

books.title: Countess Ivorynn's War
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Countess Ivorynn launches a military campaign to recover her family's stolen archive from an occupied monastery. The war becomes about conquest rather than recovery.
books.notes: Wryte's longest tragedy. Critics debate whether the countess is ever truly motivated by the archive.

books.title: The Shame of Duke Proboscorn
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Duke Proboscorn discovers his son has sold the family's genealogical records to pay gambling debts. The duke must decide whether to disown his heir.
books.notes: Greyprob's most popular tragedy. Revived frequently for its portrait of paternal conflict.

books.title: Baron Trumpfeld's Oath
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: A baron swears to never allow his archive to be cataloged by the Crown. His resistance becomes a rebellion that endangers his entire province.
books.notes: Written during Crown consolidation of archives. Banned until 1688.

books.title: Lady Tuskara's Penance
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Lady Tuskara accidentally destroys a sacred manuscript while attempting to restore it. She dedicates her life to recreating it from memory and fragments.
books.notes: Greyhorn's final completed work before her death. The restoration scenes are technically detailed.

books.title: The Corruption of Viscount Mammorex
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Viscount Mammorex accepts bribes to alter census records. His corruption spreads to other officials until the entire bureaucracy is compromised.
books.notes: Tuskfall's most cynical work. Shows corruption as a kind of social contagion.

books.title: Count Dermoth's Library
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Count Dermoth builds the finest library in the realm but refuses to stock it with books. The empty halls become a symbol of his fear of knowledge.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's most symbolic tragedy. The library is both magnificent and hollow.

books.title: The Exile of Duchess Trundale
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Duchess Trundale is exiled for publishing her family's private correspondence. Her actions expose hypocrisy but destroy her social standing.
books.notes: Wryte examines the price of truth-telling. The duchess is both heroic and foolish.

books.title: Lorde Ivortusk's Succession
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Lorde Ivortusk's three children fight over who will inherit the family archive. Their dispute reveals that each has a different understanding of family history.
books.notes: Greyprob's late masterwork. Each sibling's version of history is given equal weight.

books.title: The Burning of Baron Tuskvale
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Baron Tuskvale orders his archive burned to prevent it from revealing his father's treason. The fire spreads beyond his control.
books.notes: Temberton's most visceral tragedy. The fire imagery is overwhelming and relentless.

books.title: Countess Greymont's Trial
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Countess Greymont is tried for treason after she refuses to surrender forbidden texts to the Crown. The trial becomes a debate on intellectual freedom.
books.notes: Greyhorn's most autobiographical work. She herself was investigated for possessing banned books.

books.title: The Lies of Viscount Pachowell
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Viscount Pachowell maintains his power through a web of falsified documents. When one scribe threatens to expose him, the entire system begins to collapse.
books.notes: Tuskfall's examination of systematic deception. The viscount is both villain and victim of his own lies.

books.title: Duke Mammordale's Folly
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Duke Mammordale attempts to create a complete archive of all knowledge in the realm. His ambition bankrupts the treasury and exhausts his archivists.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's longest tragedy. The cataloging scenes are both tedious and hypnotic.

books.title: Lady Trunkshire's Rebellion
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Trunkshire leads a revolt of provincial archivists demanding better pay and recognition. Her movement threatens the established order of record-keeping.
books.notes: Wryte's most radical tragedy. Inspired actual labor movements among scribes.

books.title: The Grief of Baron Probwell
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Baron Probwell mourns his wife by obsessively archiving every moment they shared. His grief transforms into an archive that consumes his present life.
books.notes: Greyprob's most moving tragedy. The archiving becomes a form of paralysis.

books.title: Count Tuskborn's Secret
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Count Tuskborn hides a secret room containing documents that prove his family's noble status is fraudulent. Discovery looms as renovations begin.
books.notes: Temberton's most suspenseful tragedy. The tension builds through architectural details.

books.title: Duchess Dermalyne's Choice
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Duchess Dermalyne must choose between saving her children or her archive from a flood. The play explores what we value most when all cannot be preserved.
books.notes: Greyhorn's final work, published posthumously. The choice is presented without judgment.

books.title: The Ambition of Lorde Trumpmore
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Lorde Trumpmore fabricates ancient documents to prove his family descended from kings. His forgeries are so convincing that scholars accept them as genuine.
books.notes: Tuskfall's last major work. Questions whether accepted history is simply successful forgery.

books.title: Viscount Greyhorn's Reckoning
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Viscount Greyhorn conducts an audit of his estate's records and discovers decades of embezzlement. The investigation implicates his closest friends.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's final tragedy, completed weeks before her death. The audit scenes are grimly detailed.

books.title: The Patience of Baron Ivorstone
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Baron Ivorstone waits forty years for permission to access the Royal Archive. His life becomes entirely about waiting for knowledge that may never come.
books.notes: Wryte's most experimental tragedy. Structured around scenes of waiting and bureaucratic delay.

books.title: Countess Pachorina's Debt
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Countess Pachorina inherits massive debts along with her family's archive. Creditors demand the archive as payment, forcing her to value documents against survival.
books.notes: Greyprob's penultimate tragedy. Economic pressures drive the entire plot.

books.title: The Mercy of Duke Tuskdale
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Duke Tuskdale pardons a scribe who stole documents to feed his family. The mercy is seen as weakness, encouraging further thefts throughout the realm.
books.notes: Temberton's final tragedy. Explores how compassion can have unintended consequences.

books.title: Lady Mammoselle's Revolution
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Lady Mammoselle proposes opening all private archives to public access. Her radical vision threatens centuries of noble privilege and secrecy.
books.notes: Published in the year of Tuskfall's death. Considered dangerously progressive for its era.

books.title: The Vanity of Lorde Probmont
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Lorde Probmont commissions flattering histories and destroys unflattering ones. His carefully constructed legacy crumbles when hidden documents surface.
books.notes: Mammorthorn satirizes the vanity of historical revision. The lord controls everything except truth.

books.title: Baron Trunwell's Apprentice
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Baron Trunwell trains a brilliant young archivist who surpasses him in skill. Jealousy leads the baron to undermine his protege's work.
books.notes: Wryte's study of mentorship turned toxic. The apprentice remains loyal despite mistreatment.

books.title: Viscount Dermachus's Plague
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Viscount Dermachus quarantines his archive during a plague, refusing entry even to dying scholars seeking medical texts. The quarantine prevents both infection and healing.
books.notes: Greyprob's final tragedy, written after the plague of 1678. The moral dilemma remains unresolved.

books.title: The Testament of Duchess Tuskmere
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Duchess Tuskmere's will divides her archive among her children, but the distribution is unequal. The perceived favoritism destroys family bonds.
books.notes: Temberton's posthumous publication. The will itself is performed as a dramatic reading.

books.title: Count Greymarsh's Flood
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Count Greymarsh's archive is destroyed by flooding. He attempts to recreate it from memory, but each reconstruction differs from the last.
books.notes: Published posthumously. Questions the reliability of memory as preservation.

books.title: Lady Ivorwealth's Catalog
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Lady Ivorwealth becomes so obsessed with cataloging her collection that she stops reading the books themselves. The catalog becomes more important than the knowledge.
books.notes: Tuskfall's satire of bibliographic obsession. The catalog entries are performed as verse.

books.title: The Surrender of Baron Mammorage
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Baron Mammorage surrenders his archive to invaders without resistance. His pragmatism saves lives but earns him the label of coward.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's examination of survival versus honor. The baron's choice is both wise and shameful.

books.title: Lorde Tuskminster's Judgment
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lorde Tuskminster sits in judgment over a scribe accused of altering records. The trial reveals that the lord himself ordered the alterations.
books.notes: Wryte's late masterwork. The trial structure allows for dramatic irony and reversal.

books.title: Duchess Probelle's Ransom
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Duchess Probelle's archive is held for ransom by bandits. She must choose between paying and bankrupting her estate or losing centuries of family history.
books.notes: Greyprob's final published work. The ransom negotiation spans the entire play.

books.title: The Isolation of Viscount Pachwell
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Viscount Pachwell seals himself in his library to preserve it from war. Years pass, and he becomes unable to leave his self-imposed prison.
books.notes: Temberton's claustrophobic masterpiece. The library becomes both sanctuary and tomb.

books.title: Countess Trunmoor's Alliance
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Countess Trunmoor forms an alliance with rival houses to protect archives from royal seizure. The alliance fractures when members begin hoarding rather than sharing.
books.notes: Greyhorn's political tragedy. Explores how common cause can dissolve into self-interest.

books.title: Duke Ivorheart's Legacy
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Duke Ivorheart spends his fortune creating an archive to ensure his legacy. After his death, no one visits it, and his name is forgotten anyway.
books.notes: Tuskfall's meditation on the futility of legacy-building. The final scene shows an empty archive.

books.title: Baron Greythorn's Spy
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Baron Greythorn plants a spy in a rival's archive but falls in love with the intelligence the spy provides. His addiction to secrets becomes all-consuming.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's espionage tragedy. Knowledge becomes an addictive substance.

books.title: Lady Trumpshire's Donation
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Trumpshire donates her archive to a university, only to watch scholars misinterpret and misuse her family's documents. Her generosity breeds distortion.
books.notes: Wryte questions whether sharing knowledge always improves it. The scholars are well-meaning but incompetent.

books.title: The Conspiracy of Count Probshire
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Count Probshire uncovers a conspiracy among archivists to falsify records across multiple houses. His investigation makes him the next target.
books.notes: Greyprob's conspiracy thriller. The paranoia escalates throughout the play.

books.title: Viscount Mammoth's Mirror
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Viscount Mammoth creates a second archive identical to his first, then forgets which is the original. His search for authenticity consumes him.
books.notes: Temberton's most philosophical tragedy. Questions what makes a document authentic.

books.title: The Wisdom of Duchess Greyvault
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Duchess Greyvault possesses perfect memory and considers archives unnecessary. When she suffers a head injury, centuries of oral knowledge vanishes instantly.
books.notes: Greyhorn's tragedy of memory. The duchess's arrogance about her gift proves fatal to knowledge.

books.title: Lorde Tuskworth's Commission
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Lorde Tuskworth commissions an official history of his reign. The historian he hires is too honest, revealing truths the lord wanted buried.
books.notes: Tuskfall explores the conflict between truth and flattery in historical writing.

books.title: Baron Dermastone's Pact
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Baron Dermastone makes a pact with neighboring houses to destroy all evidence of a shared scandal. Each house betrays the pact for individual advantage.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's tragedy of failed cooperation. Trust crumbles under self-interest.

books.title: Countess Ivorlyn's Apprentices
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Countess Ivorlyn trains twelve apprentice archivists but teaches each a different cataloging system. After her death, they cannot work together.
books.notes: Wryte's tragedy of incompatible methods. The countess's divided teaching creates permanent discord.

books.title: The Restoration of Duke Trunbridge
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Duke Trunbridge attempts to restore damaged documents but his techniques cause more harm than the original damage. His interventions accelerate decay.
books.notes: Greyprob's cautionary tale about restoration. Good intentions worsen the problem.

books.title: Lady Pachowell's Truth
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Lady Pachowell discovers documents proving her entire family history is fabricated. She must decide whether to reveal the truth or maintain the fiction.
books.notes: Temberton's exploration of identity and documentation. The lady's crisis is existential.

books.title: Viscount Greymont's Census
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Viscount Greymont conducts an honest census despite knowing it will reveal his province's weakness to enemies. His integrity invites invasion.
books.notes: Greyhorn's tragedy of honesty. The viscount chooses truth over security.

books.title: The Fragments of Baron Mammorwell
books.author: Elara Tuskfall
books.summary: Baron Mammorwell's archive is partially destroyed, leaving only fragments. He becomes obsessed with filling the gaps, inventing history to complete the narrative.
books.notes: Tuskfall examines how loss leads to fabrication. The baron cannot tolerate incompleteness.

books.title: Duchess Trumpvale's Children
books.author: Vira Mammorthorn
books.summary: Duchess Trumpvale's seven children each claim rightful inheritance of her archive. Their legal battle destroys more documents than any fire.
books.notes: Mammorthorn's final completed tragedy. The legal proceedings are devastating in their pettiness.

books.title: Count Tuskvern's Silence
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Count Tuskvern takes a vow of silence after reading a forbidden text. His muteness protects the secret but destroys his ability to govern.
books.notes: Wryte's study of silence as both protection and paralysis. The count never speaks after the opening.

books.title: Lorde Probdale's Fire
books.author: Silas Greyprob
books.summary: Lorde Probdale's archivist starts a small fire to destroy incriminating documents. The fire spreads, consuming innocent records along with the guilty ones.
books.notes: Greyprob's tragedy of uncontrolled consequences. Selective destruction proves impossible.

books.title: The Competition of Duchess Ivormaine
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Duchess Ivormaine hosts a competition to find the best archivist in the realm. The competition becomes cutthroat, with contestants sabotaging each other's work.
books.notes: Temberton's satire of professional rivalry. The contestants destroy more than they preserve.

books.title: Viscount Trunvale's Confession
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Viscount Trunvale confesses on his deathbed to falsifying records for fifty years. His confession forces every house to question their documented histories.
books.notes: Greyhorn's devastating final tragedy. The confession undermines an entire era of record-keeping.
